name: Why does cabin trim deteriorate faster in the Denver and Front Range foothills?

mainEntity.name: Why does cabin trim deteriorate faster in the Denver and Front Range foothills?

acceptedAnswer.text: In the Denver metro and Front Range foothills, high solar UV radiation combined with intense freeze-thaw cycles causes exterior wood trim to expand, contract, and dry out rapidly. Mountain sunlight degrades protective stains quickly, leaving raw wood vulnerable to snow melt and wind-driven rain. Moisture enters tiny cracks, freezes overnight, and forces boards to split or detach from log joints. Regular inspection and routine resealing of trim perimeters help safeguard the structure against rapid foothill weather shifts.
acceptedAnswer.description: High UV exposure combined with rapid freeze-thaw cycles dries out wood finishes and expands cracks, accelerating moisture damage and wood rot in foothill areas.
